arxiv-2109-05747.title: Honey or Poison? Solving the Trigger Curse in Few-shot Event Detection via Causal Intervention
arxiv-2109-05747.creator: Jiawei Chen, Hongyu Lin, Xianpei Han, Le Sun
arxiv-2109-05747.description: Abstract Event detection has long been troubled by the trigger curse : overfitting the trigger will harm the generalization ability while underfitting it will hurt the detection performance. This problem is even more severe in few-shot scenario. In this paper, we identify and solve the trigger curse problem in few-shot event detection (FSED) from a causal view.

arxiv-2110-03307.title: Subtrees and BC-subtrees of maximum degree ≤ k \leq k in trees Journal: Theoretical Computer Science
arxiv-2110-03307.creator: Yu Yang, Xiao-xiao Li, Meng-yuan Jin, Long Li, Hua Wang, Xiao-Dong Zhang
arxiv-2110-03307.description: Abstract The subtrees and BC-subtrees (subtrees where any two leaves are at even distance apart) have been extensively studied in recent years. Such structures, under special constraints on degrees, have applications in many fields. Through an approach based on generating functions, we present recursive algorithms for enumerating various subtrees and BC-subtrees of maximum degree ≤ k \leq k in trees.

arxiv-2112-04586.title: Monolithic Integration of Quantum Resonant Tunneling Gate on a 22nm FD-SOI CMOS Process
arxiv-2112-04586.creator: Imran Bashir, Dirk Leipold, Elena Blokhina, Mike Asker, David Redmond, Ali Esmailiyan, Panagiotis Giounanlis, Hans Haenlein, Xutong Wu, Andrii Sokolov, Andrew K. Mitchell, Dennis Andrade-Miceli, Robert Bogdan Staszewski
arxiv-2112-04586.description: Abstract The proliferation of quantum computing technologies has fueled the race to build a practical quantum computer. The spectrum of the innovation is wide and encompasses many aspects of this technology, such as the qubit, control and detection mechanism, cryogenic electronics, and system integration.

arxiv-2207-14278.title: Rapid determination of single substitutional nitrogen N 0 s {}_{s}^{0} concentration in diamond from UV-Vis spectroscopy
arxiv-2207-14278.creator: T. Luo, L. Lindner, R. Blinder, M. Capelli, J. Langer, V. Cimalla, F. A. Hahl, X. Vidal, J. Jeske
arxiv-2207-14278.description: Abstract Single substitutional nitrogen atoms N 0 s {}_{s}^{0} are the prerequisite to create nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers in diamonds. They serve as the electron donors to create the desired NV - center, provide charge stability against photo-ionisation, but also are the main source of decoherence.

arxiv-2306-12768.title: Concept-aware clustering for decentralized deep learning under temporal shift
arxiv-2306-12768.creator: Marcus Toftås, Emilie Klefbom, Edvin Listo Zec, Martin Willbo, Olof Mogren
arxiv-2306-12768.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Marcus Toftås, Emilie Klefbom, Edvin Listo Zec, Martin Willbo, Olof Mogren. Decentralized deep learning requires dealing with non-iid data across clients, which may also change over time due to temporal shifts. While non-iid data has been extensively studied in distributed settings, temporal shifts have received no attention. To the best of our knowledge, we are first with tackling the novel and challenging problem of decentralized learning with non-iid and dynamic data.

arxiv-2407-09281.title: Predicting and Understanding Human Action Decisions: Insights from Large Language Models and Cognitive Instance-Based Learning
arxiv-2407-09281.creator: Thuy Ngoc Nguyen, Kasturi Jamale, Cleotilde Gonzalez
arxiv-2407-09281.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated their capabilities across various tasks, from language translation to complex reasoning. Understanding and predicting human behavior and biases are crucial for artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted systems to provide useful assistance, yet it remains an open question whether these models can achieve this.

arxiv-2409-03555.title: Unified Framework for Pre-trained Neural Network Compression via Decomposition and Optimized Rank Selection
arxiv-2409-03555.creator: Ali Aghababaei-Harandi, Massih-Reza Amini
arxiv-2409-03555.description: Abstract Despite their high accuracy, complex neural networks demand significant computational resources, posing challenges for deployment on resource constrained devices such as mobile phones and embedded systems. Compression algorithms have been developed to address these challenges by reducing model size and computational demands while maintaining accuracy. Among these approaches, factorization methods based on tensor decomposition are theoretically sound and effective.

arxiv-2507-10505.title: Signatures of Odd-Parity 𝒔 s -wave 𝚵 ∗ \Xi^{*} States in Femtoscopic Correlation Functions
arxiv-2507-10505.creator: Jia-Xin Lin, P. Encarnación, Miguel Albaladejo, Albert Feijoo

pmc-11306175.title: Increasing cotton lint yield and water use efficiency for subsurface drip irrigation without mulching
pmc-11306175.creator: Nan-nan Li, Jun-hong Li, Xiao-juan Shi, Feng Shi, Yu Tian, Jun Wang, Xian-zhe Hao, Hong-hai Luo, Zhan-biao Wang
pmc-11306175.description: IntroductionPlanting without mulching can eliminate the residual film pollution caused by the long-term use of plastic film covers, but it will increase soil moisture evaporation and heat loss and severely reduce water use efficiency and cotton productivity in cotton (Gossypium hirsutum L.) fields in arid regions.

pmc-11516095.title: Personality and Biomarkers of Neurodegeneration and Alzheimer’s Disease in Swedish Older Adults
pmc-11516095.creator: J Molinder, D Vetrano, H Zetterberg, K Blennow, M Waern, L Johansson, H Falk Erhag, R Sigström, I Skoog
pmc-11516095.description: BackgroundPersonality is associated with dementia risk. Neuroticism and conscientiousness may be involved in resistance and resilience to Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) pathology (ADP). These traits have also been associated with unspecific biomarkers of neurodegeneration; glial fibrillary acidic protein (GFAP) and neurofilament light (NfL). This study explores the role of personality in cognitive ageing.

pmc-11683236.title: Profiling low-mRNA content cells in complex human tissues using BD Rhapsody single-cell analysis
pmc-11683236.creator: Alexandra Scheiber, Manuel Trebo, Annabella Pittl, Isabel Heidegger, Theresa Hautz, Rupert Oberhuber, Zlatko Trajanoski, Florian Augustin, Sieghart Sopper, Dominik Wolf, Andreas Pircher, Stefan Salcher
pmc-11683236.description: SummaryThe successful recovery of immune cells, particularly those with low mRNA content, by single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) remains a significant challenge. Tissue dissociation and selection of the appropriate scRNA-seq technology are crucial. Our protocol efficiently recovers low-mRNA content immune cells using the BD Rhapsody scRNA-seq platform.

pmc-12416204.title: The ABC type fucose operon regulated by XtrSs through CcpA contributes to Streptococcus suis survival in macrophages
pmc-12416204.creator: Song Liang, Yumin Zhang, Shidan Zhang, Qiankun Bai, Xinming Pan, Jianan Liu, Qibing Gu, Huochun Yao, Guangjin Liu
pmc-12416204.description: Streptococcus suis (S. suis), an important zoonotic pathogen, poses a huge threat to the pig industry and human health. The fucose operon (FCS) is found in many bacteria that utilize host glycosylation modifications, contributing to bacterial growth and infection. We previously discovered that the virulence associated streptococcal transcriptional regulator XtrSs could downregulate FCS transcription.

pmc-12486292.title: Longitudinal relation between childhood maltreatment and problematic internet game use among Chinese early adolescents: The roles of internalizing symptoms and FKBP5 gene variation
pmc-12486292.creator: Xue Gong, Jianhua Zhou
pmc-12486292.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundResearch has demonstrated that childhood maltreatment is a significant predictor of problematic internet game use in adolescents. However, the underlying mechanisms of this relation, particularly the mediating processes and gene-environment interactions (G × E), remain insufficiently understood. This study employed a multi-informant, longitudinal design within a G × E framework to examine the mediating role of internalizing symptoms in the relation between childhood maltreatment and problematic internet game use.

pmc-12745450.title: Autophagic regulation of CD8+ T cell metabolic reprogramming defines acute and latent phases of cytomegalovirus infection in vivo
pmc-12745450.creator: Hui Liu, Xiaobing Liu, Wai Ho Oscar Yeung, Jiang Liu, Kevin Tak Pan Ng, Kwan Man
pmc-12745450.description: Understanding the immunoregulatory mechanism during cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection may help to combat CMV reactivation in immunocompromised or immunosuppressed individuals. Here we developed a CMV infection model in immunocompetent Sprague Dawley (SD) rats with Priscott strain and explored the cross-talk between autophagic dynamics and metabolism alterations in CD8+ T cells post infection.

pmc-13039453.title: Clinical outcomes and risk factors of cytomegalovirus reactivation in teclistamab-treated multiple myeloma patients
pmc-13039453.creator: Hira Cheema, Asis Shrestha, Syed Naqvi, Sanjay Muttineni, Sasya Dronavalli, Jawad Alrawabdeh, Marah Alzu’bi, Carolina D Schinke, Sharmilan Thanendrarajan, John D Shaughnessy, Fenghuang Zhan, Maurizio Zangari, Frits van Rhee, Samer Al Hadidi
pmc-13039453.description: Teclistamab, a bispecific T-cell engager targeting BCMA and CD3, has demonstrated efficacy in relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma but may increase infection risk due to immunosuppression. Cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation is a concern in immunocompromised patients, yet its incidence and clinical significance in teclistamab-treated patients remain poorly characterized.

pmc-13356899.title: Understanding poor sleep in emerging adulthood: the role of pre-sleep cognitive processes in daily life
pmc-13356899.creator: Alexander Ariu, Andrea H Meyer, Simone Munsch, Nadine Messerli-Bürgy
pmc-13356899.description: Study ObjectivesTheoretical perspectives suggest that pre-sleep cognitive processes, including cognitive arousal, rumination, and stress can impair sleep. However, previous studies have relied on cross-sectional designs, limiting insight into how these cognitive processes relate to sleep on a night-to-night basis. In addition, anticipatory stress has received little empirical attention, despite its relevance for poor sleep.
